responsibility: `rustc_traits` supplies rustc’s externally organized trait- and type-related query providers: `lib.rs` defines the crate’s role, wires all of its queries into `rustc_middle::query::Providers`, and re-exports selected type-operation entry points for other compiler components. Its root query files implement the compiler-facing operations around the trait system and type reasoning: `evaluate_obligation.rs` answers the legacy canonical predicate-evaluation query; `implied_outlives_bounds.rs` computes implied outlives bounds for a type in a canonical parameter environment; `dropck_outlives.rs` computes drop-check outlives results and destructor-driven constraints for ADTs; `normalize_erasing_regions.rs` normalizes generic arguments and erases regions for region-insensitive consumers; `normalize_projection_ty.rs` performs canonical normalization of projection- and alias-like types; and `type_op.rs` provides the canonical type-operation queries used to ascribe user types, prove predicates, and normalize several value forms while managing the resulting obligations. In addition, the `chalk` module integrates Chalk-based trait solving into this query crate: `chalk/mod.rs` drives end-to-end evaluation of canonical rustc goals through Chalk, `chalk/lowering.rs` converts between rustc and Chalk representations of types, predicates, goals, substitutions, and binders, and `chalk/db.rs` exposes `TyCtxt` facts through Chalk’s database and unification interfaces. Together, these pieces make `rustc_traits` the crate that packages and exposes rustc’s trait solving, normalization, outlives, drop-check, and type-operation queries—bridging compiler clients to both the traditional trait-selection machinery and the Chalk-based solver infrastructure.
